acceptance_criteria: check_inputs and check_oid_consistency pass all listed tests; zero dependencies on crypto
close_reason: added check_inputs and check_oid_consistency to pkix-path
description:
Implement two pre-loop checks inside validate_path, extracted as testable private functions.

## What

### check_inputs(chain, anchors) -> Result<()>
- chain.is_empty() -> Err(Error::NoTrustedPath) [or add EmptyChain variant per PKIX-e9v]
- anchors.is_empty() -> Err(Error::NoTrustedPath)

### check_oid_consistency(chain) -> Result<()>
RFC 5280 §4.1.1.2: the outer signatureAlgorithm field MUST equal the inner
TBSCertificate.signature field. Check every cert in the chain before calling
the SignatureVerifier. Return Err(Error::SignatureInvalid { index }) on mismatch.
Oracle: openssl verify rejects such certs.

## Tests (all using externally-generated DER hex literals — never code-under-test as oracle)
- empty chain -> Err
- empty anchors -> Err
- chain of 1 with outer OID != inner OID at index 0 -> SignatureInvalid { index: 0 }
- chain of 3 with mismatch at index 1 -> SignatureInvalid { index: 1 }
- chain of 3 all consistent -> Ok(())

## Notes
Pure logic, no crypto. Can be implemented and tested before any signature backend exists.
title: pkix-path: input guards and outer/inner OID consistency
